Good afternoon, Senator ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and honorable
members of the Committee on Health and Human Services. My name is Adam Bloom-Paicopoios. I am a resident of Wells and am proud to serve as the Executive
Director of the Alliance for Addiction and Mental Health Services, Maine (the Alliance). The Alliance is the statewide association representing Maine's community-
based behavioral health agencies who provide much-needed mental health and
substance use services to over 80,000 children, adults, and families annually. The Alliance advocates for the implementation of sound policies and evidence-based practices that serve to enhance the quality and effectiveness of our behavioral
health care system.
On behalf of the Alliance, I am here today to speak in favor of LD 63, talk about the potential of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs), and to highlight
the importance of supporting Representative Graham's companion bill to LD 63 (LR 1272) that would provide $2 million in additional funding to enable the full implementation of the program for all five existing and pre-approved CCBHCs across the state.
CCBHCs are a transformative and bipartisan approach to community behavioral health that receive flexible funding to provide expanded access to comprehensive, high-quality mental health and substance use services. CCBHCs have also been shown to be effective at generating cost savings in states across the country, including states such as Missouri and Oregon, through timely access to care and reductions in emergency department utilization, hospitalizations, and law enforcement encounters.`
In Maine, this impact has already begun to be realized through grant-funded CCBHCs that have improved access to care and experienced workforce enhancements across the state from York County up to Aroostook County. To date, our CCBHCs have reported increases in serving children, veterans, and active-duty service members. 75% of CCBHCs in Maine reported an increase in access to substance use disorder treatment. And CCBHCs have been able to begin improving access to mobile crisis response services and collaboration with 988 and the Maine Crisis Line.
This summer, Maine was announced as one of 10 states awarded entry to the federal
Medicaid CCBHC demonstration, joining neighboring New Hampshire and Vermont
as well as a diverse array of states such as Alabama, Kansas, Indiana, and Rhode island. in addition to establishing sustainable funding through Medicaid, the program enables states to receive an enhanced Federal Medical Assistance

Percentage (FMAP) for CCBHC services. For Maine, our projected enhanced FMAP for CCBHCs will be roughly 73% -- in other words, for each dollar spent by Maine on CCBHCs, the federal government will pay
73 cents. While LD 63 represents an important first step towards implementing this program, it is not
enough on its own to ensure that all pre-approved CCBHCs can participate in the demonstration. That is why I respectfully urge the committee to not only support LD 63 today, but to also support LR 1272 when it reaches this committee. LR 1272 would not only provide $2 million in additional state funding for the CCBHC demonstration, but it would generate nearly $1.5 million in federal match that combined would enable all five CCBHCs to participate in the program. Without this crucial additional funding, the Alliance is very concerned that not all CCBHCs will be able to maintain existing services when grants expire,
let alone solidify and expand their impact-- particularly in key populations and areas of high need, such as children, veterans, those with substance use treatment needs, and our rural areas.
At a moment when Maine's behavioral health system has experienced meaningful progress over the last several years, we cannot afford to take a step back and miss the opportunity to significantly enhance
access to services for Mainers across the state. I would be happy to answer any questions from the Committees. Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony this afternoon.
Respectfully,

Before the Health and Human Services Committee
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and fellow members of the Joint Standing Committee
on Health and Human Services, I am Representative Annie Graham and I am here to present LD 63, An Act to Support Implementation of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic
Projects.
As many of you know, I have been a long-time supporter of the work of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) in Maine. When I leamed that the Department had been
selected as one of 10 states to participate in the federal Medicaid CCBHC Demonstration, I was
thrilled. I believe this work will be transformational because it will ensure a continuum of community-based behavioral health services are available throughout the state. For these reasons, I was happy to sponsor this bill for the Department.
LD 63 is simple. It requires funding that was already appropriated for CCBHCs in Public Law
2023, chapter 643 to be used to support the Medicaid services state share of funds needed for state--licensed mental health organizations to participate in the Demonstration Program. Currently, the $2 million in allocated funds are in a non-Medicaid account and cannot be utilized
by the Office of MaineCare Services for the state share component of CCBHC reimbursement to
providers. Without legislative approval to transfer these already allocated funds to the proper
account, the Department will be unable to continue the important work they've begun.
I hope that you will join me in supporting this initiative. We must ensure that our constituents
have access to these comprehensive behavioral health services.
The Department will follow my testimony and provide further information. They can answer any
questions you may have. Thank you for your consideration.

Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, distinguished members of the Health and Human Services committee, my name is Dale Hamilton and I am the executive director of Community Health and
Counseling Services. I am here to speak in favor of LD 63, An Act to Support Implementation of
Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic Projects.
CHCS was one of the first Maine recipients of a SAMHSA CCBHC grant. We have been involved with the implementation of CCBHC services since 2021. The CCBHC structure shifts the mental health and
substance use disorder services system away from a fee-for-service environment and towards a cost-based
system. We have seen the promise of improved access, quality and coordination provided by this model.
The hard work of Maine's Department of Health and Human Services and various stakeholders resulted
in Maine being selected to participate in the CMS CCBHC demonstration project.
This emergency legislation simply transfers existing designated CCBHC funding, appropriated by the
legislature, to support the transition of this model to the demonstration project. The model provides an opportunity to expand resources in ways that have not been achieved for decades. For example, our organization is prepared to expand on-site resources in under resourced areas such as Northern Penobscot and Piscataquis counties. This includes the addition of medication management services. This is made possible by the model design and funding methodology. The integrated design and outcome focused approach, presents an opportunity for Maine to realize the same positive results achieved in other states.
CCBHC serves all ages and supports the development of services for specialized populations such as Veterans. Under the CCBHC structure, we will continue to offer 7-day access to children and families for
urgent walk-in care needs. The walk-in resource has provided immediate support to children and families experiencing a disruptive event. As a result of this access, families have reported that they were able to avoid utilization of the emergency department as a means to address their situation. This is an example of how the model can flexibly deliver services that improve outcomes and lower costs.
LD 63 is critically important to get this model stood up by the planned implementation date of March 1,
2025. The demonstration project provides an opportunity for the Department of Health and Human
Services to build on the work that has been achieved to date. The inherent nature of demonstration
projects is that they are not perfect and often need modifications to achieve optimal results. There will be
opportunities to strengthen the model by resolving some of the early challenges. Representative Graham
is sponsoring LR 176 An Act to Support the Full Implementation of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics in the State. This bill provides one-time funding that enables all five approved CCBHC's in Maine to maintain operations while transitioning to a CCBHC structure.
In closing, I ask that you continue to support the implementation of CCBHC's in Maine by endorsing LD 63. It seems reasonable to move dedicated CCBHC funding to the purpose that will move implementation
forward.
Sincerely,

POSITION STATEMENT IN SUPPORT
LD 63: An Act to Support Implementation of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic Projects
As the state's largest grassroots mental health advocacy organization, NAMI Maine supports the passage of LD 63: An Act to Support implementation of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic Projects. NAMI Maine represents the 1 in 4 l\/lainers who struggle with mental health challenges each year. Mental Illness is a complex journey, with individuals waiting an average of 10 years from the onset of symptoms until
they seek treatment.
According to the World Health Organization, suffering from a serious mental illness has been found to reduce life expectancy anywhere from 13-32 years, depending on location and access to services. in most
Western countries, WHO states that mental illness is the leading cause of disability, as well as accounting
for 30-40% of sick days. Currently, suicide is the second leading cause of death for 10-24-year-olds, and it is the 10"` leading cause of death across all ages. The most recent data released by the State of Maine
was from 2022, with the number ofsuicide deaths at 277, meaning we lose a Mainer to suicide on average
every 31.5 hours.
Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics, or CCBHCs, provide much-needed care within the communities and have been found to reduce burdens and use of higher levels of care, such as hospitalizations and incarcerations. The nine required components of CCBHCs include 24/7 mobile crisis teams and crisis stabilization, Screening, assessment, and diagnosis, Patient-centered treatment planning, Outpatient mental health and substance use sen/ices, Primary care screening and monitoring of key health indicators, Targeted case management, Psychiatric rehabilitation services, Peer and family support, and lastly tailored mental health care for members of the armed forces and veterans. Additionally, CCBHCs must adhere to set criteria regarding the timeliness of access, care coordination, quality reporting, staffing, and scope of sen/ices. Because of this, CCBHCs have been found to increase access to behavioral health services and needed resources across all ages, particularly high-risk populations.
We have been informed that Maine is facing significant budget challenges. With this in mind, NAMI Maine
will advocate for continued access to life-changing and life-saving behavioral health programming. The nearly 500 Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics in 46 states have demonstrated that this is a cost-effective and best-practice program to invest in due to diversion from higher and more costly levels
of care. Because of this, NAMI Maine strongly urges the passage of LD 63, An Act to Support Implementation of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic Projects.
ABOUT NAMI MAINE: Incorporated in 1984, the National Alliance on Mental Illness, Maine Chapter (NAM! Maine)
is the state's largest grassroots mental health organization. With support from national and regional affiliates, the agency is dedicated to building better lives for everyone impacted by behavioral health concerns. NAMI Maine engages with leaders and community partners at all levels to improve the state's mental health system through collaboration and education.

Testimony of the Office of Behavioral Health
Maine Department of Health and Human Services
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services
In support of LD 63, An Act to Support Implementation of Certified Community Behavioral
Health Clinic Projects
Sponsor: Representative Graham

Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Health and Human Services, my name is Sarah Squirrell, and I serve as the Director of the Office of Behavioral Health (OBH) in the Maine Department of Health and Human Services. I am here today to testify in support of LD 63, An Act to Support Implementation of Certified Community
Behavioral Health Clinic Projects.
The intent of this bill is to ensure that necessary funding for Maine's participation in the federal
Section 223 Medicaid Ceitified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC) Demonstration receives requisite legislative approval. Public Law 2023, Chapter 643 (Supplemental Budget)
allocated $2 million in one-time funding for "the startup and implementation costsfor
community behavioral health organizations participating in the CCBHC projects previously
funded byfederal grantsfrom the US Department ofHealth and Human Services ' Substance
Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration" .
The allocated funds are currently in a non-Medicaid account and cannot be utilized by the Office
of MaineCare Services for the state share component of CCBHC reimbursement to providers, a
requirement of the federal Demonstration program. The Department seeks legislative approval
and carrying language pursuant to Title 5, Section 1582 for the CCBHC model implementation. Without legislative approval through LD 63 to transfer the previously allocated funds to an
Offlce of MaineCare Services Medicaid account, the Department would be unable to implement
the Section 223 Medicaid CCBHC Demonstration program utilizing the funds as the requisite
state share.
The Department supports this legislation as a key and essential initiative to further strengthen the continuum of community based behavioral health services and to expand access to comprehensive and integrated behavioral health care services throughout the state. Maine was
approved to participate in the federal Medicaid CCBHC Demonstration through a new cohort of
just ten states to join the existing eight participating states, providing enhanced federal match

rate equal to Maine's Children's Health Insurance Program federal match which alleviates
significant financial burden of CCBHC service delivery on the State.
The Department's efforts to implement CCBHCs in Maine represents a transformational
opportunity for the State of Maine to advance a continuum of care across the lifespan that can provide comprehensive and integrated mental health, substance use and peer recovery services.
CCBHCs provide integrated, evidence based, trauma-informed, recovery-oriented and person-
and family-centered care. The model will improve availability and access to the full array of
CCBHC required community based behavioral health services, including outpatient mental
health and substance use services, case management services, psychiatric rehabilitation services, peer support and family and caregiver supports, physical health screening and monitoring, and
care for uniformed Service Members and Veterans. CCBHC's will further enhance and improve
the screening, assessment and diagnosis process for individuals seeking services with a preliminary triage and identification of routine, urgent and crisis needs which will facilitate
timely access to CCBHC services in addition access to care coordination and the development of
comprehensive treatment plans within 60 days.
The impending implementation of Maine's CCBHC model was included in the Office of Behavioral Health's Motion to Resolve the Consent Decree and the CCBHC model includes core
elements of the Department's recent negotiated settlement with the Department of Justice with the aim of strengthening the array of community based services to children and youth, ensuring
timely access to those services supporting youth in the least restrictive settings in their home and
community. Additionally, CCBHCs will allow for the provision of High Fidelity Wraparound
services and other evidence-based models of care for children, youth and families. The design of Maine's model aligns with the goals of Maine's Mental Health Rights of Recipients; more specifically, the right to a service system that employs culturally normative services, the right to coordination of the disparate components of the community service system, and the right to a comprehensive array of services to meet the recipient's needs.
Providers certified as part of Maine's CCBHC Demonstration Program implementation have already begun developing their clinic infrastructure through federal SAMHSA CCBHC Clinic-
level grants to become CCBHCs. However, until Maine implements the Demonstration, there is
no reimbursement method available to fully implement the CCBHC model in Maine outlined as
part of our application unless additional funds are appropriated. The original purpose of this
funding request was to ensure our SAMHSA CCBHC grantee providers were able bridge a
potential gap in funding should they not be successful in receiving additional federal funds prior
to State implementation. However, we are happy to report all participating providers have
received necessary federal grant funding to maintain their CCBHC infrastructure as the
Department prepares to launch the Demonstration program.
The issue this bill seeks to address is a real concern as CCBHCs are paramount to expanding
comprehensive and coordinated behavioral health care services throughout the state, including
more underserved communities who may currently lack other comparable services and resources.
Maine was one of ten states in the last CCBHC demonstration cohort and addressing these
funding complications is necessary for the Department to proceed with the project. If unable to

use these funds for the required state share, Maine would also be the first state nationally to withdraw from the Demonstration program prior to implementation.
In conclusion, this minor adjustment in allocation will have a substantial impact toward successfully improving upon the behavioral health care in Maine, providing more services and resources, and greater support to our communities.
Thank you for your time and attention. I would be happy to answer any questions you may have and to make myself available for questions at the work session.
Sarah Squirrell

Good Afternoon, Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and esteemed members of the Health and Human Services Committee,
My name is Simonne Maline. I am the Executive Director for the Consumer Council System of Maine (CCSM). I am writing today on behalf of the CCSM to testify in favor of L.D. 63: "An Act to Support Implementation of Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic Projects."
The Consumer Council System of Maine is a public instrumentality written into State Statute by the Maine Legislature to serve in an advisory capacity and to provide legislators with guidance and advice regarding the delivery of effective and appropriate adult mental health services from those served by them.
We are strong supporters of the CCBHC model nearing full implementation and have been supporting this model for many years as it has grown across the country. We see the potential this model has to support the people of Maine in new and innovative ways.
The reason for our support is that this model has many pieces that peers have been asking for in so many ways. Some examples are access regardless of ability to pay, access to peer support, for people with Medicare only, they have never had access to basic case management services and will be able to now. Trauma-informed services are vitally important as is revitalizing treating co-occurring conditions! Veterans will also have access to services outside of Togus as well.
We have partnered with DHHS on this initiative in multiple ways over the past 2 years.
We are excited that this work is also going to greatly increase people with lived experience having a voice with organizations boards of directors. This part of the CCBHC project is partially owned by the CCSM, as we have been active participants in curriculum development and educate our peers about the model and bringing awareness to the potentials the model affords.
We as an organization typically do not weigh in on funding bills but we support any and all efforts needed to get this new model of behavioral healthcare into full fruition.
In closing we urge to vote "Ought to Pass" on LD 63.
Thank you for reading our testimony today.
Sincerely,
